thread:
Sam L: Quick FYI — ran a batch of perf runs against main w/ expandable_segments=on, max_split_size_mb=64, garbage_collection_threshold=0.8. Saw fewer small alloc stalls but a spike in OOMs on long KV-heavy traces.
Maya R: Can you paste the repro command and logs? was it the tiled-attn kernel change we landed yesterday?
Sam L: repro: `python -m perf_runner --model redwood-v2 --seq 4096 --kv-warmup 200 --iters 500` and then `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 python ...` logs show `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` during attention forward at step ~342.
Linus K: Interesting — that sequence length + kv-warmup will fill the workspace quickly. Did you also enable workspace reuse in the runtime flags?
Sam L: yes `--enable-workspace-reuse` was on. Profile shows large number of small free/alloc churns from KV cache slices. nvprof snapshot:
```
AllocMetric: peak 48.3GB
FreeMetric: many 1-4MB frees
Top op: attention_forward (seq 4096, batch 1)
```
Jordan: That churn screams fragmentation. max_split_size_mb=64 might be too big, causes fewer splits and larger contiguous allocations that can't be reused.
Maya R: Try lowering `max_split_size_mb` to 16-32 and reduce `garbage_collection_threshold` to 0.6 so GC runs earlier. Also experiment with `expandable_segments=false` — that prevents ever-growing segments that leave tiny holes.
Devon: Quick note: turning off expandable_segments may increase total peak but reduce fragmentation. We saw this pattern in the last KV warmup run with batching heuristics tuned.
Sam L: Ran a sweep: expandable_segments=false, max_split_size_mb=32, gc_threshold=0.6. Result: peak mem +2GB but OOMs disappeared, tail latency stable, and throughput +4% under 32-token batching. Will upload perf graphs.
Maya R: Nice. Can you attach the flame graph and the allocator event trace? also add the run id to the perf board.
Sam L: Uploaded to /perf/runs/1712349999-alloc-sweep (flame.svg, alloc_events.json). Run id: perf-1712349999. Flame shows most time in `attention_kernel_v2` and many small allocations during KV slice copy.

Linus K: I'll own the canary. Action items: 1) create small reproducer that triggers KV churn (Sam), 2) run matrix for {max_split_size_mb:16,32,64} x {expandable:true,false} (Devon), 3) add an allocator trace event hook to correlate with kernel selection (Maya). I'll post results in this thread. :eyes:
Sam L: sounds good. thanks all. :thumbsup:
